2:13.t: "The Baals", "the Ashtaroth", "the Asherahs": Baal was the Canaanite storm god, Ashtoreth (plural Ashtaroth) a goddess, and the Asherahs wooden poles honoring the goddess Asherah. The KJV's "groves" in 3:7 means these poles.

3:7.t: "The Baals", "the Ashtaroth", "the Asherahs": Baal was the Canaanite storm god, Ashtoreth (plural Ashtaroth) a goddess, and the Asherahs wooden poles honoring the goddess Asherah. The KJV's "groves" in 3:7 means these poles.

3:16.t: KJV: "a dagger which had two edges, of a cubit length".

3:31.t: "Oxgoad": a long pointed stick used to drive oxen.

6:24.t: "Yahweh-shalom": the KJV prints "Jehovah-shalom", "the LORD is peace" (see the Style guide on names built on Jehovah).

8:26.t: KJV: "a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold".

9:4.t: "Pieces of silver": the KJV does not name the unit; if shekels, 70 pieces would be about 800 grams and 1,100 pieces about 12.5 kilograms (as 17:3 shows).

16:5.t: "Pieces of silver": the KJV does not name the unit; if shekels, 70 pieces would be about 800 grams and 1,100 pieces about 12.5 kilograms (as 17:3 shows).

17:2.t: "Pieces of silver": the KJV does not name the unit; if shekels, 70 pieces would be about 800 grams and 1,100 pieces about 12.5 kilograms (as 17:3 shows).

11:30.t: Readers disagree over whether Jephthah offered his daughter as a burnt offering or dedicated her to lifelong service at the sanctuary, unmarried. The text says he "did to her as he had vowed" and stresses that she never knew a man.

12:6.t: Shibboleth means "ear of grain" or "stream". The Ephraimites could not say the "sh" sound.

13:5.t: "Nazirite": the KJV's "Nazarite", one set apart to God by a vow: no wine, no razor, no contact with the dead (Numbers 6). Samson's vow was for life.

13:18.t: "Wonderful": Hebrew peli, from the same root as "Wonderful" in Isaiah 9:6, meaning beyond understanding.

17:3.t: KJV: "eleven hundred shekels of silver". 17:4: "two hundred shekels". 17:10: "ten shekels of silver".

18:30.t: "Manasseh": the Hebrew text writes Moses with a small raised letter added to make Manasseh, probably to spare Moses' name the shame of an idolatrous grandson. Some ancient copies read Moses.

19:1.t: "Concubine": a wife of lower rank, here called his wife and him her husband (19:3).

19:2.t: "Was unfaithful": the KJV's "played the whore against him". The Greek translation reads "became angry with him", which fits her going home to her father.

19:18.t: "The house of the LORD": the tabernacle at Shiloh. The Greek translation reads "my house".

19:22.t: "Worthless men": the KJV's "sons of Belial", Hebrew for worthless or wicked people. "Have sex with him": the KJV's "that we may know him", meaning sexual relations, as in Genesis 19:5.

20:13.t: "Worthless men": the KJV's "sons of Belial", Hebrew for worthless or wicked people. "Have sex with him": the KJV's "that we may know him", meaning sexual relations, as in Genesis 19:5.

19:30.t: The Greek translation adds the Levite's message, telling those he sent to say this to all Israel.

20:16.t: "At a hair": the KJV's "at an hair breadth".

20:18.t: "Bethel": the KJV's "the house of God", which is what Bethel means. The ark was there at that time (20:27).

20:26.t: "Bethel": the KJV's "the house of God", which is what Bethel means. The ark was there at that time (20:27).

20:31.t: "Bethel": the KJV's "the house of God", which is what Bethel means. The ark was there at that time (20:27).

21:2.t: "Bethel": the KJV's "the house of God", which is what Bethel means. The ark was there at that time (20:27).

20:22.t: "The army": the KJV's "the people", as often in battle accounts.

20:35.t: The two totals (25,100 and 25,000) differ because 20:46 gives a round number.

20:46.t: The two totals (25,100 and 25,000) differ because 20:46 gives a round number.

21:22.t: "Do us a favor": the KJV's "be favourable unto them for our sakes". The fathers had not given their daughters, so they had not broken the oath of 21:1.

21:25.t: The closing line repeats 17:6 and frames chapters 17-21.

2:16.t: "Judges" (Hebrew shophetim, from shaphat, "to judge, govern"): these leaders did more than settle disputes. They were deliverers raised up by God to rescue Israel and then lead it, which is why the book also calls them "deliverers" or "saviors" (3:9, 3:15). Only Deborah is shown hearing cases (4:5).

6:12.t: "The angel of the LORD": a messenger who speaks as the LORD Himself (6:14, 6:16), as in Genesis 16:7-13. Gideon and Manoah fear they will die because they have seen God (6:22, 13:22). Pronouns for the angel stay lowercase, as in Genesis.
